subject: Access mode selection: VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN (EdgeCorp pilot)

Subject: Pilot connectivity: deciding between peering, PrivateLink, or S2S for EdgeCorp -> Redwood Private

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. We're kicking off a small pilot (internal analytics + PII tokenization) and want to lock the networking approach before the infra spin-up. Our main constraints:
- No public exposure of inference endpoints.
- Minimal changes to our VPC address plan (we have legacy 10.0.0.0/8 blocks in several accounts).
- Predictable latency to the Redwood pods (we're in us-west-2).
- Auditability for flow logs & ability to prove no egress to the public internet for compliance.

High-level ask: can you summarize tradeoffs between VPC Peering, PrivateLink (interface endpoints), and a site-to-site VPN for this pilot and recommend one for a 2-team PoC?

I've attached a short checklist of our compliance gating items.

Cheers,
Sarah

Cloud Architect, EdgeCorp

Subject: Re: Pilot connectivity: deciding between peering, PrivateLink, or S2S for EdgeCorp -> Redwood Private

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear constraints. Quick summary below; Ben (networking) is cc'd and will add technical notes. We should pick an approach for the PoC today so infra can provision.

Short summary / recommendation (TL;DR):
- PrivateLink: best isolation and simplest security posture for a multi-account customer where you want to avoid routing changes and limit blast radius. Slightly more complex for NAT/egress considerations and requires endpoint ENIs + SG rules. Good for short-term PoC where you want per-service access control and no transitive routing.
- VPC Peering: low-latency, fewer middleboxes, but requires non-overlapping IP spaces and manual route table management; not transitive across multiple peers. Best if EdgeCorp can dedicate a clean CIDR or use a dedicated VPC for Redwood traffic.
- Site-to-site VPN: fastest to stand up if you already have an appliance, supports NAT traversal for overlapping IPs (via NAT), but adds variable latency and operational overhead; harder to tie to per-service RBAC and endpoint-level observability.

Based on your constraints (legacy 10.* overlaps + strong auditability requirement), my provisional recommendation for the PoC: PrivateLink, unless you can carve out a dedicated peering VPC (preferred from latency/cost perspective). If latency variance becomes an issue we can fall back to peering.

Next steps: Ben will drop a short matrix with metrics (latency, implementation ETA, ops burden) and a checklist of what we need from EdgeCorp (subnets, security contacts, expected qps).

- Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot connectivity: deciding between peering, PrivateLink, or S2S for EdgeCorp -> Redwood Private

Hi all — adding the technical tradeoff matrix (condensed) and practical playbook items. I'm keeping it short so the PoC can move.

Tradeoff matrix (Peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN):
- Latency: Peering (lowest, L3 direct) > PrivateLink (small ENI hop + SG checks) > VPN (variable; dependent on appliance & tunnels).
- IP overlap: Peering (rejects overlap) / PrivateLink (works regardless; endpoint ENIs are in our VPC) / VPN (works if you NAT, but NAT adds complexity).
- Transitivity: Peering (no transitive routing) / PrivateLink (no transitive) / VPN (can be routed but usually manual).
- Security scoping: PrivateLink (per-service permissions, SGs) > Peering (per-subnet route control) > VPN (broad network-level unless filtered).
- Observability / Auditability: PrivateLink (flow logs on ENIs + VPC flow logs) ~= Peering (VPC flow logs + route tables) > VPN (depends on tunnel logging and on-prem tooling).
- Operational complexity: Peering (low once IP space sorted) / PrivateLink (medium: endpoints & policies) / VPN (high: tunnel uptime, MTU, BGP if used).
- Cost: Peering (data transfer patterns matter) / PrivateLink (hourly endpoint + data processing per-GB charges) / VPN (appliance + egress costs).

Practical PoC playbook (what I need from EdgeCorp):
1) Confirm if you can provide a small dedicated VPC CIDR (e.g., /24) for a peering VPC — this avoids overlap issues. If yes, peering gives best latency/cost.
2) If not, confirm whether creating interface endpoints in your VPC is allowed by security (we ask for two AZs worth of endpoints).
3) If you're forced to use your existing VPCs and can't create endpoints, we'll stand up an s2s VPN and use NAT to avoid IP overlap issues; expect higher latency.
4) Provide security contact (for SG updates) and a cloud admin with rights to create endpoints/peers.
5) We'll run a short synthetic latency test once connectivity is provisioned (p95 token gen on standard prompt).

I've attached a short "peering-ip-overlap-playbook.md" and an S2S snippet with our PSK example (remove PSKs for production). Also note: PrivateLink avoids egress through the public internet by design but you still need to lock down outbound rules on your side if any callbacks exist (model telemetry, metrics).

I'll be available for a 30-min call today at 2pm PT if you want to walk the options.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Network Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: s2s-config-snippets.txt, peering-ip-overlap-playbook.md

Thanks — quick note from a compliance/contract perspective before EdgeCorp signs off:
- PrivateLink is easiest to document in an SOC2 context because access can be scoped per-service; the audit trail is clearer.
- If we use peering, we need a short addendum documenting CIDR commitments and a rollback plan (we've seen customers change internal VPCs mid-project).
- For VPNs we should document the expected SLO (tunnel flaps) and include an operational runbook for toggling to a different path.

For the pilot, if EdgeCorp can accept the PrivateLink hourly endpoint charges and create two endpoints (one per AZ), that minimizes an initial security review and should keep the procurement path simple. If they prefer peering we will require a /24 committed CIDR and a signed network-change notice.

Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager, Enterprise & Compliance
Redwood Inference

- Redwood: we'll share the endpoint service name, a small SG template, and the short test harness (p95 token latency test). Ben will open a support ticket to reserve capacity in the us-west-2 cluster for the PoC.
- Legal/Proc: Kimberly to confirm any procurement notes for endpoint hourly charges (we think it's small, procurement prefers charge to be on their cloud bill).

I'll put together a short runbook and drop it into the shared Drive link. Meeting notes + the checklist are attached.

Thanks — moving to PrivateLink for the PoC.

- Jasmine
